scenario: A laptop's battery drains quickly and the case is starting to bulge. What should the technician do?

options.text: Stop using it and replace the battery safely
Charge it overnight to recalibrate it
options.note: A swollen battery is a fire risk.

options.text: Press the case flat and keep using it

explanation: Swollen lithium-ion batteries can catch fire. Power down, remove carefully and dispose of it according to local regulations.

scenario: Which memory module form factor is used in most laptops?
explanation: Small outline DIMMs are shorter than desktop DIMMs.

scenario: A user can tap phones to a payment terminal to pay. Which technology is used?
explanation: Near-field communication works at a few centimeters for payments and pairing.

scenario: A user wants to connect wireless earbuds to a phone. Which technology is typically used?
explanation: Pair the devices, then enter a PIN or confirm the code if prompted.

scenario: A laptop screen is very dim, but an image is faintly visible with a flashlight. What has most likely failed?

options.note: Dead pixels wouldn't leave a faint full image.
A cable fault usually causes no image or flicker.

explanation: A faint image means the LCD works but isn't lit. LED backlights or older CCFL inverters can fail.

scenario: A touchscreen registers touches in the wrong place. What should be tried first?
explanation: If calibration doesn't help, the digitizer may need replacement.

scenario: Which feature lets a phone share its cellular internet connection with a laptop?
explanation: Hotspots share data over Wi-Fi, USB or Bluetooth and may use the data plan quickly.

scenario: A company wants to push apps, enforce passcodes and remotely wipe employees' phones. What should it use?

options.note: Protects data but doesn't push apps or wipe remotely.

explanation: MDM enforces policies; mobile application management (MAM) can manage just company apps on personal devices.

scenario: Which connector is reversible and used on most modern Android phones and many laptops?
explanation: USB-C can carry data, power (USB PD), video and Thunderbolt on supported devices.

scenario: A laptop needs to connect to multiple monitors, wired network and a keyboard with one cable at a desk. What fits?

options.note: Adds USB ports only, too slow for displays.
Mirrors a screen; no network or keyboard ports.

explanation: Docks and port replicators extend a laptop's ports.

scenario: A laptop gets very hot and shuts down while gaming. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Blocked vents or a failing fan

explanation: Clean vents with compressed air and check that the fan spins.

scenario: A laptop's Wi-Fi is weak after the display was replaced. What should be checked?

options.text: The antenna cables in the lid

options.note: Signal weakened after hardware work, not software.

explanation: Laptop Wi-Fi antennas usually run through the display bezel.

scenario: A phone's battery drains quickly after installing a new app. What should be checked first?
explanation: Rogue apps or background activity can drain batteries; malware is also possible.

scenario: Which wireless standard provides connectivity for a phone when no Wi-Fi is available?
explanation: Cellular networks connect phones to carrier data networks.

scenario: Users want their calendar, contacts and email on both phone and computer. What should be configured?
explanation: Sync uses accounts like Microsoft 365, Google or iCloud.

scenario: Which laptop component is usually replaced to fix a keyboard with several dead keys?
explanation: First check for debris, drivers or liquid damage; otherwise replace the keyboard.

scenario: A user's laptop doesn't detect any Wi-Fi networks. What should be checked first?

options.text: Whether the drive is nearly full
Whether the DNS server is set
Whether the firewall is blocking it

explanation: Many laptops have a function key or switch that disables wireless radios.

scenario: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
explanation: Common ports: 20/21 FTP, 22 SSH, 23 Telnet, 25 SMTP, 53 DNS, 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS, 3389 RDP.

scenario: Which port is used by Remote Desktop Protocol?
explanation: RDP lets users control a Windows computer remotely.

scenario: Which protocol and port provide encrypted remote command-line access?
explanation: Use SSH instead of Telnet because Telnet sends everything in clear text.

scenario: Which ports does DNS use?
explanation: DNS uses UDP 53 for most queries and TCP 53 for larger responses and zone transfers.

scenario: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices?
explanation: DHCP uses UDP ports 67 (server) and 68 (client).

scenario: Which protocol is used to send email between mail servers?
explanation: SMTP uses port 25 between servers; clients often submit mail on 587.

scenario: A user wants email to stay synced across phone and laptop, with folders kept on the server. Which protocol fits?

options.note: Usually downloads and removes mail from the server.

explanation: IMAP uses port 143 (993 for IMAPS).

scenario: Which Windows file sharing protocol uses port 445?
explanation: Server Message Block shares files and printers on Windows networks.

scenario: A Windows PC shows an IP address of 169.254.12.5. What does this mean?

options.text: It couldn't reach a DHCP server
It has a valid public IP address

explanation: APIPA addresses (169.254.0.0/16) are self-assigned when DHCP fails.

scenario: Which is a private IPv4 address?
What does a default gateway do?
explanation: The default gateway is usually the router's IP address on the local network.

scenario: Which device connects multiple devices on a LAN and forwards traffic based on MAC addresses?

options.note: Forwards between networks using IP addresses.

explanation: Switches learn which MAC addresses are on which ports.

scenario: Which device connects a home network to the ISP's cable or DSL line?
explanation: Many home devices combine a modem, router, switch and access point.

scenario: Which device provides Wi-Fi to wireless clients and connects them to a wired network?
explanation: APs bridge wireless clients to the wired LAN.

scenario: Which twisted-pair cable category supports 10 Gbps up to 100 meters?
explanation: Cat6 supports 10 Gbps only up to about 55 meters.

scenario: Which connector is used on Ethernet twisted-pair cables?
explanation: RJ45 is an 8-pin modular connector.

scenario: Cable must run through the air space above a drop ceiling used for ventilation. Which type should be used?

options.note: Gives off toxic smoke when burning.

explanation: Plenum jackets produce less toxic smoke and meet fire codes for air-handling spaces.

scenario: Which cable type is best for long distances and is immune to electromagnetic interference?
explanation: Fiber carries light; single-mode reaches farther than multimode.

scenario: Which connector is used on coaxial cable for cable TV and cable modems?
explanation: RG6 cable with F-type connectors is common for cable internet.

scenario: Which Wi-Fi standard is Wi-Fi 6 and can use 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz (and 6 GHz for 6E)?
explanation: Wi-Fi 7 is 802.11be.

scenario: Which wireless band offers more channels and higher speeds but shorter range?
explanation: Higher frequencies are absorbed more by walls.

scenario: Which wireless security protocol is the most secure for a home network?
explanation: WPA3-Personal uses SAE to resist offline password guessing.

scenario: Which DNS record maps a hostname to an IPv4 address?
explanation: TXT records hold text such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC email settings.

scenario: Which DNS record type is used for email authentication settings like SPF?
explanation: SPF, DKIM and DMARC help prevent email spoofing.

scenario: Which network type covers a building or campus?
explanation: A WAN connects LANs over long distances.

scenario: A small office wants a firewall, routing and Wi-Fi in one device. What fits?
explanation: Small office/home office routers combine many network functions.

scenario: Which protocol monitors and manages network devices like switches and printers?
explanation: SNMP uses ports 161 and 162.

scenario: What does NAT do on a home router?

options.text: Lets private devices share one public IP

explanation: Network address translation maps private addresses to the router's public address.

scenario: Which IPv6 address type is automatically configured on every interface and starts with fe80?
explanation: Link-local addresses work only on the local network segment.

scenario: Which tool would a technician use to attach wires to a patch panel?
explanation: Punchdown tools seat wires into 110 or Krone blocks.

scenario: Which tool attaches an RJ45 connector to the end of a cable?
explanation: Follow the T568A or T568B pinout consistently.

scenario: Which component stores data only while the computer is powered on?
explanation: RAM is volatile; storage drives keep data when power is off.

scenario: How many pins does a DDR4 desktop memory module have?
explanation: DDR4 and DDR5 DIMMs both have 288 pins but are keyed differently, so they aren't interchangeable.

scenario: A user installs two identical RAM modules in matching colored slots. What benefit does this give?

options.note: Memory channels don't affect the SSD.

explanation: Dual channel increases memory bandwidth; check the motherboard manual for the right slots.

scenario: Which type of RAM detects and corrects single-bit errors and is common in servers?
explanation: The motherboard and CPU must support ECC.

scenario: Which storage interface gives the fastest performance for an SSD in an M.2 slot?
explanation: M.2 slots can support SATA or NVMe; check which the motherboard and drive use.

scenario: Which RAID level stripes data across disks for speed but provides no redundancy?
explanation: If any disk in RAID 0 fails, all data is lost.

scenario: Which RAID level mirrors data on two disks?
explanation: RAID 1 survives one disk failure.

scenario: What is the minimum number of disks for RAID 5?
explanation: RAID 5 stripes data with distributed parity and survives one disk failure.

scenario: Which RAID level combines mirroring and striping and needs at least four disks?
explanation: RAID 10 offers good performance and redundancy.

scenario: Which power supply connector provides the main power to a modern motherboard?
explanation: CPUs get extra power from a 4- or 8-pin EPS connector.

scenario: Which voltages does a standard ATX power supply provide?
explanation: The 12 V rail powers the CPU and GPU through regulators.

scenario: A new graphics card needs more power than the PSU can provide. What should be done?

options.text: Add more RAM to the system

explanation: Check the GPU's recommended PSU wattage and required PCIe power connectors.

scenario: What should be applied between a CPU and its cooler?
explanation: Thermal compound fills microscopic gaps for better heat transfer.

scenario: Which firmware interface replaced legacy BIOS and supports Secure Boot and large GPT disks?
explanation: UEFI supports Secure Boot, GPT partitions and faster startup.

scenario: A PC loses its date and time whenever it's unplugged. What should be replaced?

options.note: PC still works when plugged in.

explanation: The coin-cell battery keeps firmware settings and the clock when power is off.

scenario: Which chip stores encryption keys and supports BitLocker and Windows 11 security features?
explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0.

scenario: Which video connector carries both digital audio and video and is common on TVs?
explanation: DisplayPort also carries audio and video and is common on PCs and monitors.

scenario: Which port can provide display, data and charging through a single cable and supports very high speeds on many laptops?
explanation: Thunderbolt 3, 4 and 5 use the USB-C connector.

scenario: Which printer type uses heat on special paper, commonly for receipts?
explanation: Direct thermal printers need heat-sensitive paper.

scenario: A business needs to print multipart carbon forms. Which printer type fits?
explanation: Impact printers strike a ribbon hard enough to print on multiple layers.

scenario: In a laser printer, which step melts toner onto the paper?

options.note: Writes the image with a laser.

explanation: Steps: processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning.

scenario: Which component in a laser printer is extremely hot and should be allowed to cool before servicing?
explanation: The fuser uses heat and pressure to bond toner to paper.

scenario: Which expansion slot is used by modern graphics cards?
explanation: PCIe x1 slots are used for smaller cards like some NICs and sound cards.

scenario: A user needs to add USB ports and wired networking to a desktop. Which component could be installed?
explanation: Expansion cards add ports or functions.

scenario: Which input device converts handwriting or drawings into digital input?
explanation: Touchscreens also use digitizers.

scenario: Which device lets one keyboard, monitor and mouse control several computers?
explanation: KVM stands for keyboard, video and mouse.

scenario: Which type of drive has spinning platters and moving read/write heads?
explanation: HDD speeds are often 5,400 or 7,200 RPM.

scenario: A technician must work inside a PC. What protects the components from static discharge?
explanation: Use an ESD strap and mat, and handle components by their edges.

scenario: Which CPU feature lets one physical core run two threads at once?
explanation: Simultaneous multithreading improves throughput for multithreaded workloads.

scenario: Which BIOS/UEFI setting must usually be enabled to run virtual machines efficiently?
explanation: Hypervisors rely on hardware virtualization extensions.

scenario: A user wants a printer that everyone on the network can use. How should it be connected?

options.text: By USB to one user's laptop
options.note: Only that laptop can print easily.
Not practical for sharing with everyone.

explanation: Network printers can be shared directly; USB printers can be shared through a computer.

scenario: Which hypervisor type runs directly on hardware without a host operating system?

options.note: Runs as an app on a host OS.

explanation: Examples: VMware ESXi and Microsoft Hyper-V. Type 2 examples: VirtualBox and VMware Workstation.

scenario: A developer wants to test software in an isolated VM on their Windows laptop. Which hypervisor type fits?
explanation: Type 2 hypervisors such as VirtualBox run on top of the existing OS.

scenario: Which is a common use of virtual machines?

options.text: Increasing the size of a monitor

explanation: VMs also run legacy software and consolidate servers.

scenario: Which cloud service model provides ready-to-use applications such as webmail?
explanation: Software as a service: the provider manages everything except users and data.

scenario: Which cloud service model provides virtual servers, storage and networking that the customer manages?
explanation: Infrastructure as a service gives the most control.

scenario: Developers want to deploy code without managing the operating system. Which model fits?
explanation: Platform as a service handles the OS, runtime and scaling.

scenario: A cloud is shared by several organizations with the same compliance needs, such as hospitals. Which model is this?
explanation: Community clouds share costs among organizations with common concerns.

scenario: Which cloud characteristic means resources automatically grow and shrink with demand?
explanation: Elasticity helps handle traffic spikes without overpaying.

scenario: Which cloud characteristic means customers are billed based on usage?
explanation: Usage is measured and billed, like a utility.

scenario: What is multitenancy in cloud computing?

options.text: Many customers share the same infrastructure
Each app runs in its own region

explanation: Providers isolate tenants logically while sharing physical resources.

scenario: A company provides employees with Windows desktops hosted in the cloud and accessed from any device. What is this?

options.note: Follows a user between PCs, but the desktop isn't hosted.

explanation: Cloud VDI is sometimes called desktop as a service (DaaS).

scenario: Which is a benefit of containers compared with virtual machines?

options.text: They start faster and use fewer resources
They each include a full guest OS
options.note: VMs do; containers share the kernel.

explanation: Containers package an app with its dependencies and share the host OS kernel.

scenario: Users want files on their laptop to automatically match the copies stored in the cloud. Which feature fits?
explanation: Services like OneDrive keep files synced across devices.

scenario: Which minimum resources must a host have to run several VMs smoothly?

options.note: VMs run on the host's local resources.

explanation: Each VM consumes host CPU, memory, storage and network resources.

scenario: What is the first step of the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology?

options.text: Establish a theory of probable cause

explanation: Steps: identify the problem; establish a theory; test it; plan and implement; verify and add preventive measures; document.

scenario: After fixing a problem, what should a technician do before documenting?

options.text: Establish a theory of probable cause
Close the ticket and inform the user

explanation: Make sure everything works and help prevent the issue from happening again.

scenario: A technician's first theory turns out to be wrong. What should they do next?

options.text: Establish a new theory or escalate
Tell the user nothing can be done

explanation: If a theory isn't confirmed, form a new one or escalate.

scenario: When establishing a theory of probable cause, which approach is recommended?

options.text: Start with the most expensive part
Replace the most likely part first

explanation: Simple causes like an unplugged cable are common.

scenario: A PC makes a series of beeps and shows nothing on screen at startup. What do the beeps indicate?

options.text: A DHCP scope that is full

explanation: Beep codes vary by firmware vendor; look them up for the motherboard.

scenario: A desktop shows no lights and no fans when turned on. What should be checked first?
explanation: No power at all points to the outlet, cable, PSU or front power switch connection.

scenario: A computer randomly shuts down, and the case feels hot. What is the likely cause?
explanation: Clean dust, check fans and reapply thermal paste if needed.

scenario: A hard drive makes grinding or clicking noises. What is the most likely issue?
explanation: Back up data immediately and replace the drive.

scenario: A technician smells burning near the power supply. What should they do?

options.text: Power off, unplug and replace the PSU
Keep it running to see if it stops
Open the PSU and repair it

explanation: Never open a PSU; capacitors can hold a dangerous charge.

scenario: Capacitors on a motherboard are bulging and leaking. What does this mean?

options.text: The motherboard is failing and should be replaced

explanation: Swollen capacitors cause instability and random shutdowns.

scenario: A PC shows "No boot device found." What should be checked first?

options.note: The error is already on screen.
Not needed to boot from a local drive.
Wouldn't cause a missing boot device.

explanation: Check the drive appears in UEFI, the cables are seated and the boot order is correct.

scenario: Which tool tests whether each wire in an Ethernet cable is connected correctly?

options.note: Can test continuity but not pairs easily.

explanation: Cable testers detect opens, shorts and miswired pairs.

scenario: A technician needs to find which wall jack connects to which patch panel port. Which tool fits?
explanation: A tone generator puts a signal on the cable, and the probe detects it.

scenario: Which tool tests whether a network port on a NIC or switch is working?
explanation: A loopback plug sends the transmit signal back to the receive pins.

scenario: Which tool checks power supply voltages or outlet wiring?
explanation: Multimeters measure voltage, resistance and continuity.

scenario: Users report slow Wi-Fi in one area. Which tool helps find interference and channel overlap?
explanation: Analyzers show signal strength and channel usage.

scenario: Two computers show an "IP address conflict" message. What is the cause?

options.text: Two devices share one IP address
The Ethernet cable is too long

explanation: Often caused by a static IP inside the DHCP scope. Fix the static address or DHCP reservations.

scenario: A user can reach websites by IP address but not by name. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Check DNS server settings with ipconfig /all and test with nslookup.

scenario: A user has a connection to the local network but no internet. Which setting should be checked?
explanation: Without a correct gateway, traffic can't leave the local subnet.

scenario: A network connection drops intermittently. The cable runs next to fluorescent lights and motors. What is a likely cause?

options.note: Wouldn't depend on nearby lights and motors.

options.text: A DHCP scope that is full

options.note: Causes steady slowness, not EMI-related drops.

explanation: Reroute the cable, use shielded cable or switch to fiber.

scenario: Wi-Fi is slow, and many nearby networks use the same 2.4 GHz channel. What should be done?

options.text: Use a less crowded channel or 5 GHz
Switch to WEP for faster speed

explanation: Use non-overlapping channels 1, 6 or 11 on 2.4 GHz.

scenario: A laser printer prints faint, repeated images of earlier content on the page. What is this called and what's the likely cause?

options.text: Speckling from a dirty paper tray
Low ink in an inkjet cartridge

options.note: Drivers cause garbled output, not ghost images.

explanation: Replace the imaging drum or fuser as indicated.

scenario: Toner smears off the page when touched. Which laser printer part is most likely failing?
explanation: The fuser melts toner onto the paper.

scenario: An inkjet printer produces streaks or missing lines. What should be done first?

options.note: Network settings don't affect print quality.

explanation: Clogged nozzles are common; then check ink levels.

scenario: A printer shows garbled characters on every page. What is the likely cause?

options.note: Causes jams or skewed pages, not garbage text.

explanation: Reinstall the correct driver for the printer model.

scenario: Paper keeps jamming in a laser printer. What should be checked?

options.note: Spooler issues stop printing, not cause jams.

explanation: Worn rollers or damp, wrong-size paper often cause jams.

scenario: A monitor shows no image, but the PC is running. What should be checked first?

options.note: The PC runs, so first check the cable and input.

explanation: Check that the monitor is on the right input and cables are seated.

scenario: A RAID 5 array shows a degraded status. What does this mean?

options.text: One drive failed; data is still available
All data on the array has been lost
The array is rebuilding faster than usual

explanation: Replace the failed drive promptly so the array can rebuild.

scenario: A system boots, but Windows reports far less RAM than installed. What should be checked?

options.text: That RAM is seated and compatible

explanation: Reseat RAM, check slots and confirm module compatibility.

scenario: A new SSD isn't shown in File Explorer but appears in Disk Management as unallocated. What should be done?

options.text: Enable the drive in Device Manager

options.note: The new drive has no file system yet.

explanation: New drives need partitions and a file system before use.

scenario: A laptop's display flickers when the lid is moved. What is the likely cause?
explanation: The display cable runs through the hinge and can wear.

scenario: Which device shows a hex code on a motherboard to help diagnose startup failures?
explanation: Many motherboards also have built-in debug LEDs or code displays.

scenario: A phone won't charge with its cable but charges with another cable. What has failed?
explanation: Isolate the problem by swapping one component at a time.

scenario: Several users on one switch lose connectivity at the same time. What is the most likely single point of failure?
explanation: Look for what the affected devices have in common.

scenario: Which step comes after testing a theory and confirming the cause?
explanation: Plan for possible effects, such as backups or change approvals, before implementing.
